title: Electric toothbrush and shaver: safe teardown
summary: Electric toothbrushes and shavers hold a small rechargeable cell or two (lithium-ion in some models, nickel-metal hydride in others), a small motor or a coil-and-magnet drive, and a charging coil. The handle is closed tight round the cell: open it only the way it was made to open (twist-off cap or screws), use plastic tools in any seam, and never put a blade or screwdriver in a seam.

steps.text: If it is on its stand, or has a cord, unplug it from the wall first. Look at the handle before you charge it or open it: a split seam, a bottom cap pushed out, a bulge, heat or a sweet chemical smell. If you find any of these, don't charge it: follow safety_swollen_lithium. If it looks sound and you want to know whether it works, first check the charger's cord and case: if either is damaged, don't plug it in (Philips EasyClean manual). Then charge the handle on its own stand on a tile or stone surface, watch it, and unplug it if it feels warm.

Run the cell down before you open the handle: take it off the stand, switch it on and let it run until it stops, and repeat until it won't start (Philips EasyClean manual). iFixit discharges the Oral-B iO below 25% before opening it, to lower the risk of a fire (iFixit iO battery).
Pull off the brush head. On a shaver or trimmer, lift off the shaving head by its frame.
steps.warn: Shaver foils, cutters and trimmer blades are sharp. Handle them by the frame and keep them in a box.

steps.text: Open the bottom the way it was made to open. Twist-off caps: the Oral-B iO's cap unlocks with a quarter turn anticlockwise, using the charger as a key (iFixit iO battery); the Philips Sonicare EasyClean's cap has a slot you turn anticlockwise; Philips names a flat-head screwdriver for this (Philips EasyClean manual). Turn it in the slot only and never prise at the seam. Pressed-in end caps, as on the Oral-B Pro 1000 and Sonicare HX6710: iFixit pries the HX6710's with a thin screwdriver (iFixit HX6710 battery), whose cap is held by two plastic tabs, and does not name a tool for the Pro 1000's (iFixit Pro 1000 battery). Use a plastic spudger instead.
steps.warn: Plastic tools only in any seam: the cell can sit just behind the bottom cap. Never push a knife, blade or screwdriver into a seam. If plastic won't open it, keep the handle whole.

steps.text: Shavers: undo the screws first (the Philips S5000 has one T9 Torx screw on the back), then unclip the housing halves with a plastic spudger, starting at the small recess (iFixit S5000). The Philips OneBlade's halves are press-fitted: grip both ends and twist them apart (iFixit OneBlade). iFixit calls this the hardest part and recommends rubber gloves, so go slowly, and if it won't give, keep the shaver whole.

Hold the toothbrush handle upside down and press the brush shaft to slide the insides out of the bottom (Philips EasyClean manual, iFixit iO battery, iFixit Pro 1000 battery). On the iO, first lift the metal ring under the cap; iFixit uses tweezers, but a plastic tool does it away from the cell (iFixit iO battery).

Look at the cell now you can see it. Swollen, dented, leaking, hot or smelly means stop and follow safety_swollen_lithium. Read its label: Li-ion or 3.6–3.7 V means lithium-ion; Ni-MH or 1.2 V means nickel-metal hydride.

Cut the cell free. In the Oral-B Pro 1000, the Sonicare HX6710 and the Philips S5000 the cell is soldered to the board (iFixit Pro 1000 battery, iFixit HX6710 battery, iFixit S5000). Cut one lead or tab at a time with flush cutters, close to the board and away from the cell, and tape each cut end before you cut the next. Where a cell sits loose in a recess, as in the Oral-B iO, ease it out with a plastic spudger (iFixit iO battery). Where it sits in a plastic carrier, as in the Philips EasyClean (the manual pries it out), push it out by hand or with a plastic tool once the tabs are cut (Philips EasyClean manual).
steps.warn: Philips' manual levers under the board with a screwdriver and iFixit desolders the tabs. Both put force or heat beside the cell, so cut instead. Wear eye protection. Keep the cell under 54 °C (130 °F) (OSHA SHIB 06-20-2019). Cut tabs are sharp.

steps.text: Measure the cell with the meter on DC volts, then tape both ends and write the reading and its chemistry on the tape.

Take the drive. In the Oral-B Pro 1000 and the Philips S5000 shaver a small motor is soldered to the board (iFixit Pro 1000 battery, iFixit S5000). iFixit desolders it. With the cell already out, you can instead cut its wires or tabs close to the board and leave a stub on the motor. The Sonicare Flexcare Platinum swings a magnet with a coil (Righto Sonicare), and other Sonicare drives differ; in the DiamondClean HX9340 two magnets are held by two screws (iFixit HX9340). The Oral-B iO's linear motor comes out after its Torx 8 screws (iFixit iO teardown).
steps.warn: Keep loose magnets away from children: two swallowed magnets can pull together through the gut.

steps.text: Leave the charging stand sealed. It is a mains device: if its cord or case is damaged, don't use it (Philips EasyClean manual).
Store lithium-ion cells part-charged, ends taped, in a metal box away from where people sleep (safety_swollen_lithium). Keep nickel cells apart from lithium ones and label which is which.

notes:
## What's worth keeping and why

- **The whole brush or shaver, if it works.** Clean teeth and a shave matter when there is no dentist or barber.
- **Lithium-ion cell.** One cell of about AA size, 3.6–3.7 V. The Sonicare HX6710 has a 3.7 V lithium-ion cell about 14 by 49 mm (iFixit HX6710 battery). The Oral-B iO has a 740 or 750 mAh lithium-ion cell, 49 by 14 mm (iFixit iO battery). The Philips S5000 shaver has a 3.7 V, 715 mAh lithium-ion cell in 14500 (AA) size (iFixit S5000). Use one in a small torch, a sensor or a LoRa node, always with a proper single-cell lithium charger board and protection.
- **Nickel-metal hydride (NiMH) cell.** 1.2 V. The Oral-B Pro 1000 has one NiMH cell, 42 by 14 mm (iFixit Pro 1000 battery). The OneBlade guide fits a 1.2 V AA NiMH cell, 1800 mAh (iFixit OneBlade). Two or three in series run small 2.4–3.6 V gear. Charge them only with a NiMH charger, never a lithium one.
- **Motor.** In rotating brushes and shavers, a tiny DC motor: a small fan, a stirrer or a vibration alert. Sonic brushes and the Oral-B iO have a coil drive instead.
- **Magnets.** The Sonicare Flexcare Platinum's drive swings a magnet with a coil in two halves (Righto Sonicare). Small strong magnets for latches and catches.
- **Charging coil.** The handle picks up power from the stand through a coil; the Flexcare Platinum charges at about 80 kHz (Righto Sonicare). The iO's coil is soldered to the bottom of its board (iFixit iO teardown). A spare small coil.
- **Charging stand.** Keep it, sealed, with a working handle.

## Variations

- **Lithium-ion:** Oral-B iO (iFixit iO battery), Sonicare HX6710 (iFixit HX6710 battery), Sonicare ProtectiveClean 4100 HX6810 (Philips HX6810 sheet), Sonicare Flexcare Platinum (Righto Sonicare), Philips S5000 shaver (iFixit S5000).
- **NiMH:** Oral-B Pro 1000 (iFixit Pro 1000 battery) and the cell iFixit fits to the Philips OneBlade (iFixit OneBlade), though that guide's introduction also mentions lithium-ion, so check the label.
- **Other models:** check the label on the cell. Don't assume a chemistry from the brand.
- **Opening:** twist-off bottom caps on the Oral-B iO and Sonicare EasyClean, pressed-in end caps on the Oral-B Pro 1000 and Sonicare HX6710, screws and clips on the Philips S5000, or press-fitted halves on the OneBlade (iFixit iO battery, Philips EasyClean manual, iFixit Pro 1000 battery, iFixit HX6710 battery, iFixit S5000, iFixit OneBlade).
- **Cell fixing:** soldered to the board in the Pro 1000, HX6710 and S5000, or sitting in a recess it lifts out of in the iO.
- **Drive:** a rotary motor in rotating brushes and shavers; a coil swinging a magnet in the Sonicare Flexcare Platinum (Righto Sonicare), and magnets held by screws in the HX9340 (iFixit HX9340); a linear coil motor in the iO (iFixit iO teardown).
- **Water:** water can seep in round the shaft over time (Righto Sonicare), and an opened shaver may no longer be water-resistant (iFixit S5000).

## Battery safety

- Philips says removing the cell can't be undone, and to protect your eyes, hands, fingers and work surface (Philips EasyClean manual). Philips' own steps twist a screwdriver under the circuit board to break the battery connections and then pry the cell from its carrier. iFixit's guides desolder the tabs (iFixit HX6710 battery, iFixit S5000). This guide cuts the tabs instead, which keeps force and heat away from the cell. It is not a maker's method, so go slowly. Work on a tile or metal tray.
- Heat above 54 °C (130 °F), dropping, crushing and puncturing damage lithium cells. Bulging, hissing, leaking, rising heat or smoke mean move the cell away from anything that burns, then into a metal container with sand (OSHA SHIB 06-20-2019).
- Never short the two ends of a cell (iFixit Pro 1000 battery).

## What to leave

- **Swollen, leaking or damaged cells.** Store them in sand outdoors (safety_swollen_lithium).
- **Handles that won't open with the cap or plastic tools.** Store them whole as a battery item.
- **The inside of the charging stand.** It is a mains device.
- **The small boards,** unless you need a spare switch or chip.
- **Corded clippers and shavers that plug straight into a socket.** They run on mains. Unplug them and leave the mains parts alone. This guide is for cordless handles.

## Testing what you got out

- **Lithium-ion cell:** above 3.0 V is a good start; 2.0–3.0 V, charge it gently and watch it; below 2.0 V, reject it. Then follow test_lithium_cell.
- **NiMH cell:** 1.2 V nominal; a freshly charged cell reads a little higher. Charge it on a NiMH charger and check that it holds its voltage for a few days.
- **Motor:** touch it briefly to a 1.2–3.7 V cell (see test_motor).
